title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
title_zh: LIBERO-PeRM：个性化机器人操作基准测试

paragraphs.en: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/ .
paragraphs.zh: 对于通用型机器人而言，个性化是其在家庭环境中实现真正实用性的关键。 尽管通用机器人操作技术已得到广泛研究，但个性化机器人操作（PeRM）却缺乏一个受控的基准，无法将任务完成与偏好满足区分开来。 我们提出了 LIBERO-PeRM，一个用于具身智能体偏好学习的基准。 LIBERO-PeRM 研究了五个问题：1）策略如何在零样本设置中遵循偏好；2）它们如何从演示中学习单一偏好；3）随着演示数量的增加，它们能多高效地获取偏好；4）学习到的偏好如何在不同布局和任务中泛化；以及 5）策略如何组合偏好并在冲突情况下表现。 我们提出了一种受控的模拟环境中可观察偏好的构建方法和分类体系，涵盖了运动、技能和用户配置文件的选择。 这种构建方法仅限于可通过语言表达的偏好，这些偏好可以在 LIBERO 中实例化而无需改变任务目标，能够自动评估，并可在不同任务中重复使用。 基于 LIBERO，我们的程序化流程可以生成包含或不包含偏好的成对演示。 我们创建了五个任务套件（共 312 个任务），包含高质量的演示、丰富的元数据和偏好满足度指标。 实验表明，当前的 VLA 策略在零样本个性化方面存在困难，而 SFT 则使偏好变得可学习。 混合训练在保留无偏好任务表现方面优于顺序自适应，并且结合上下文提示时的性能优于仅进行偏好训练的方法，但可能会削弱对运动偏好的学习；偏好泛化、分解和冲突处理仍然具有挑战性。 代码、数据集和演示可在项目网站上找到：https://libero-perm.github.io/ 。

paragraphs.en: Household manipulation has been a long-standing goal in robotics and embodied AI, with the promise of improving daily life by enabling robots to perform chores from natural language instructions (e.g., “put an apple, bread, and milk on my plate”). Recent progress in generalist robotic manipulation has been driven in large part by Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] , which show strong generalization across diverse multimodal inputs [ 5 , 6 ] and heterogeneous embodiments [ 7 , 8 ] . However, real-world deployment demands more than completing the nominal task: embodied agents must also execute tasks in ways that align with the preferences, habits, and constraints of individual users , a requirement we refer to as personalization .
paragraphs.zh: 家庭操作一直是机器人技术和具身人工智能的长期目标，它有望通过让机器人根据自然语言指令（例如，“把苹果、面包和牛奶放在我的盘子里”）执行日常事务来改善生活。 近期通用型机器人操作领域的进步，很大程度上得益于视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型 [1, 2, 3, 4]，这些模型在多样化的多模态输入 [5, 6] 和异构的具身形式 [7, 8] 中展现出强大的泛化能力。 然而，真实世界的部署需求不仅限于完成名义上的任务：具身智能体还必须以符合个体用户偏好、习惯和约束的方式执行任务，这一要求我们称之为个性化。

paragraphs.en: Preferences introduce diverse execution requirements for identical goals. For instance, placing a mug might require a specific handle orientation or a designated landing spot. Consequently, personalized manipulation must satisfy user-specific constraints on both what strategies are selected and how actions are performed. In this framework, preferences are treated as a learning dimension parallel to object-oriented task learning; the policy’s objective is to maximize preference adherence within a single trajectory without compromising fundamental task success.
paragraphs.zh: 偏好为相同目标引入了多样化的执行要求。 例如，放置一个杯子可能需要特定的把手朝向或指定的落点。 因此，个性化操作必须满足用户对所选策略及执行方式的具体约束。 在此框架中，偏好被视为与面向对象的作业学习并行的学习维度；策略的目标是在单一轨迹内最大化对偏好的遵循，同时不损害基本作业的成功率。

paragraphs.en: Nevertheless, progress on personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) remains impeded by two major gaps. First, PeRM lacks a shared formulation and standardized evaluation protocol across prior work. Existing studies define personalization through diverse problem settings, including implicit preference alignment [ 9 , 10 ] , multi-user style adaptation [ 11 ] , user-specific object-receptacle pairing [ 12 ] , and helpful action prediction [ 13 ] ; they also specify preferences through natural language [ 13 , 14 ] , few user examples [ 9 ] , explicit preference functions [ 15 ] , human speech [ 5 ] , or numerical preference vectors [ 11 ] . Evaluation is similarly fragmented, spanning task success, user studies [ 13 , 9 , 11 , 14 ] , and preference-based scoring functions [ 16 , 17 ] , making methods difficult to compare and failure modes hard to diagnose. Second, existing benchmarks typically emphasize high-level navigation or semantic selection over fine-grained manipulation preferences and multi-preference conflicts. The closest preference-based RL benchmark [ 18 ] lacks robotic preference-learning datasets and multi-preference evaluation. Other personalization benchmarks focus on object navigation or high-level receptacle selection [ 19 , 20 ] , while recent memory-based manipulation benchmarks [ 21 , 22 ] do not distinguish task-instance memorization from genuine user-preference-driven personalization.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，个性化机器人操作（PeRM）的进展仍受到两个主要差距的阻碍。 首先，先前的研究缺乏 PeRM 的统一表述和标准化评估协议。 现有研究通过多种问题设定来定义个性化，包括隐式偏好对齐 [9, 10]、多用户风格适应 [11]、用户特定的物体-容器配对 [12] 以及辅助动作预测 [13]；它们还通过自然语言 [13, 14]、少量用户示例 [9]、显式偏好函数 [15]、人类语音 [5] 或数值偏好向量 [11] 来指定偏好。 评估同样支离破碎，涵盖任务成功、用户研究 [13, 9, 11, 14] 和基于偏好的评分函数 [16, 17]，这使得不同方法难以比较，失败模式也难以诊断。 其次，现有基准测试通常更强调高层导航或语义选择，而非精细的操作偏好和多偏好冲突。 最接近的基于偏好的强化学习基准 [18] 缺乏机器人偏好学习的数据集和多偏好评估。 其他个性化基准测试则聚焦于物体导航或高层容器选择 [19, 20]，而近期的基于记忆的操纵基准测试 [21, 22] 未能区分任务实例的记忆与真正由用户偏好驱动的个性化。

paragraphs.en: To address these gaps, we introduce a novel Personalized Robotic Manipulation Benchmark ( LIBERO-PeRM ), built using the popular LIBERO [ 23 ] framework. We elevate user preferences to a fundamental building block alongside tasks and layouts. Following the taxonomy of human preferences [ 24 ] , we define a controlled taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering Motion Preference (trajectory constraints), Skill Preference (task strategies), and User Profile (semantic biases). The benchmark is restricted to preferences that can be expressed in language, instantiated without changing the original task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Within this scope, we provide 37 single-preference instances and 18 two-preference combinations.
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这些不足，我们提出了一种新颖的个性化机器人操作基准（LIBERO-PeRM），该基准基于广受欢迎的 LIBERO [23] 框架构建。 我们将用户偏好提升为与任务及布局并列的基本构建模块。 遵循人类偏好的分类体系 [24]，我们在模拟环境中定义了一套受控的可观察偏好分类体系，涵盖运动偏好（轨迹约束）、技能偏好（任务策略）和用户画像（语义偏见）。 该基准仅限于那些能够通过语言表达、在不改变原始任务目标的情况下实现、可自动评估且能跨任务复用的偏好。 在此范围内，我们提供了 37 个单一偏好实例和 18 种双偏好组合。

paragraphs.en: LIBERO-PeRM features an extensible procedural generation pipeline that automatically instantiates tasks and their preference-conditioned variants within shared layouts. To support systematic training and evaluation, the pipeline simultaneously produces explicit preference satisfaction metrics and rich subtask-level metadata, including language instructions, goal images, and physical attributes.

paragraphs.en: For benchmarking, we construct five task suites with 312 preference-conditioned tasks and pipeline-generated, human-reviewed demonstrations, each targeting a core capability in personalized manipulation (Figure 1 , top). LIBERO-SinglePref evaluates single-preference learning; LIBERO-PrefScale evaluates scaling across data sizes, tasks, and layouts; LIBERO-PrefConflict evaluates preference-preference and task-preference conflicts; LIBERO-PrefCompose evaluates multi-preference composition; and LIBERO-ComprePref evaluates realistic preference-conditioned reasoning based on contextual language. In LIBERO-PrefScale, we further provide no-preference data, unseen layouts, and different tasks to support in-domain evaluation, task/layout generalization, and preference-level generalization over different tasks in unseen layouts.
paragraphs.zh: 为了进行基准测试，我们构建了五个任务套件，包含 312 个基于偏好的任务以及通过流程生成并经人类审核的演示示例，每个套件都针对个性化操控的一项核心能力（图 1，顶部）。 LIBERO-SinglePref 评估单偏好学习；LIBERO-PrefScale 评估数据规模、任务和布局变化下的扩展性；LIBERO-PrefConflict 评估偏好间冲突以及任务与偏好间的冲突；LIBERO-PrefCompose 评估多偏好的组合能力；而 LIBERO-ComprePref 则基于上下文语言评估真实的偏好条件推理能力。 在 LIBERO-PrefScale 中，我们进一步提供了无偏好数据、未见过的布局以及不同类型的任务，以支持领域内评估、任务与布局的泛化能力，以及在未见布局中跨不同任务的偏好层面泛化能力。

sents.zh: 在 LIBERO-PrefScale 中，我们进一步提供了无偏好数据、未见过的布局以及不同类型的任务，以支持领域内评估、任务与布局的泛化能力，以及在未见布局中跨不同任务的偏好层面泛化能力。

paragraphs.en: We use LIBERO-PeRM to conduct an initial study of five key research topics in personalized manipulation (see bottom row of Figure 1 ): 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how policies learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently policies acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose multiple preferences and behave under conflicts. These topics organize our experiments and highlight the core capabilities that robots must develop for reliable personalization.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 LIBERO-PeRM 对个性化操控中的五个关键研究主题进行了初步研究（参见图 1 的底部一行）：1）策略在零样本设置中如何遵循偏好；2）策略如何从演示中学习单一偏好；3）随着演示数量的增加，策略获取偏好的效率如何变化；4）学习到的偏好在不同布局和任务中如何泛化；以及 5）策略如何组合多种偏好并在发生冲突时表现如何。 这些主题构成了我们实验的组织框架，并凸显了机器人为了实现可靠的个性化必须发展的核心能力。

paragraphs.en: Our contributions and findings are as follows:
paragraphs.zh: 我们的贡献和发现如下：

paragraphs.en: We introduce a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, together with an automated pipeline that produces preference-conditioned demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了一种受控的模拟中可观察偏好的公式和分类体系，并配套开发了一条自动化流程，该流程能够生成基于偏好的演示、丰富的元数据以及偏好满足度指标。

paragraphs.en: We construct five task suites, LIBERO-SinglePref, LIBERO-PrefScale, LIBERO-PrefConflict, LIBERO-PrefCompose, LIBERO-ComprePref, comprising 312 preference-conditioned tasks with pipeline-generated, human-reviewed demonstrations and evaluation protocols for controlled personalization studies.
paragraphs.zh: 我们构建了五个任务套件：LIBERO-SinglePref、LIBERO-PrefScale、LIBERO-PrefConflict、LIBERO-PrefCompose 和 LIBERO-ComprePref，其中包含 312 个基于偏好的任务，这些任务配有通过流程生成并经人类审核的演示示例，以及用于受控个性化研究的评估协议。

paragraphs.en: Extensive experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training improves no-preference task success relative to sequential adaptation and contextual-prompt task success and preference satisfaction relative to preference-only LoRA, but weakens motion-preference learning; broader layout diversity and matched no-preference data also help, while preference generalization, decomposition, and execution under conflicts remain difficult.
paragraphs.zh: 大量实验表明，当前的 VLA 策略在零样本个性化方面存在困难，而 SFT 则使偏好变得可学习。 混合训练相较于顺序适应方法，提升了无偏好任务的成功率；相较于仅使用偏好的 LoRA，则在上下文提示任务的成功率和偏好满足度上有所改善，但削弱了运动与偏好的学习能力。此外，更丰富的布局多样性和匹配的无偏好数据也有帮助，但在冲突情境下，偏好的泛化、分解和执行仍然具有挑战性。

paragraphs.en: Robotic Manipulation Benchmark. Many benchmarks have been developed to evaluate different aspects of robotic manipulation, including cross-embodiment generalization [ 7 , 32 , 33 ] , generalized manipulation [ 26 , 37 , 39 ] , long-horizon reasoning [ 34 , 27 , 28 , 31 ] [ 40 , 41 ] , and sim-to-real transfer [ 29 , 30 , 25 ] . Among them, LIBERO [ 23 ] has emerged as a widely adopted benchmark due to its high-quality demonstrations and standardized data generation pipeline, primarily focusing on lifelong learning and task generalization. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on task completion, without explicitly modeling user-specific preferences. In contrast, our LIBERO-PeRM targets personalized manipulation with preference-aware task suites that disentangle task success from preference satisfaction. Table 1 compares commonly used robotic manipulation benchmarks.

paragraphs.en: Personalized Robotic Manipulation. Prior work uses personalization to cover heterogeneous settings, leaving the scope of personalized manipulation unclear. Some studies frame it as trajectory-level preference alignment via human feedback, reward signals [ 10 , 42 ] [ 43 , 44 ] , RL post-training [ 45 , 46 , 47 ] [ 48 ] , or implicit preference optimization [ 49 , 50 , 51 ] . Others study multi-user style adaptation [ 11 ] [ 52 ] , object-receptacle pairing [ 12 ] , or helpful action prediction [ 13 ] . In contrast, personalized manipulation requires an operational formulation for preference-conditioned physical action. We address this gap with LIBERO-PeRM, which provides a controlled taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation and five preference-aware task suites targeting key personalization aspects.
paragraphs.zh: 个性化机器人操控。 以往的研究利用个性化方法涵盖异构场景，但个性化操控的具体范围仍不明确。 一些研究将其定义为通过人类反馈、奖励信号 [ 10 , 42 ] [ 43 , 44 ]、强化学习后训练 [ 45 , 46 , 47 ] [ 48 ] 或隐式偏好优化 [ 49 , 50 , 51 ] 实现轨迹层面的偏好对齐。 另一些研究则关注多用户风格自适应 [ 11 ] [ 52 ]、物体与容器配对 [ 12 ]，或辅助动作预测 [ 13 ]。 相比之下，个性化操控需要一种基于偏好条件的物理动作操作化表述。 我们通过 LIBERO-PeRM 填补了这一空白，该框架在模拟环境中提供了可观察偏好的受控分类体系，并包含五个针对关键个性化方面的偏好感知任务套件。

paragraphs.en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models. Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models [ 6 , 53 , 2 , 4 , 54 , 55 ] [ 56 ] have shown strong reasoning and generalization abilities by leveraging VLM backbones [ 57 , 58 , 59 ] , large-scale multimodal instruction datasets [ 60 , 61 , 62 ] , and diverse robotic datasets [ 7 , 51 , 32 , 63 ] [ 64 ] , alongside advances in VLM-based spatial reasoning [ 65 ] , policy guidance [ 66 , 67 ] , and tactile- and force-aware robot learning [ 68 ] . However, existing benchmarks [ 23 , 27 ] mainly measure task success, leaving preference alignment underexplored despite its importance for home robots, where users may specify not only what task to perform but also how it should be executed. In this work, we introduce LIBERO-PeRM, which evaluates five key personalization topics through preference-injected trajectories, natural-language preference instructions, and ground-truth preference satisfaction matrices. For hierarchical VLAs [ 69 , 70 ] , LIBERO-PeRM further provides subtask decompositions and subgoal-image annotations, covering the key signals needed to evaluate personalized manipulation.

paragraphs.en: Preference describes the relative desirability among alternatives [ 71 ] . Personalized robotic manipulation, therefore, requires a policy to select, among feasible trajectories that complete a requested task, one that also satisfies the user’s preference. A preference is a variable independent of the task goal: it constrains how the same goal is achieved rather than replacing the goal. Natural language is our interface for both variables, but this independence distinguishes the setting from merely redefining a language-conditioned task. paragraphs.en: Motion Preference . This type of preference constrains the physical properties of the trajectory while preserving task completion. For the task “put the mug on the table” , the preference “avoid a particular area of the table” induces a trajectory-level distance constraint, requiring the robot to keep the end-effector and mug away from that region during execution. We denote this kind of preference as P motion P_{\mathrm{motion}} .
paragraphs.zh: 运动偏好。 这类偏好会在保持任务完成的同时，对轨迹的物理特性施加约束。 对于“将杯子放在桌子上”这一任务，“避开桌子上的特定区域”这一偏好会引入一个轨迹层面的距离约束，要求机器人在执行过程中使末端执行器和杯子远离该区域。 我们将这类偏好表示为 P_motion P_{\mathrm{motion}}。

paragraphs.en: Building upon the LIBERO framework, LIBERO-PeRM provides an extensible procedural data-generation pipeline for preference learning and evaluation, as illustrated in Figure 3 ; model-assisted generation and validation details are given in Appendix C . The pipeline consists of three stages: (1) Preference Selection and Layout Modification; (2) Preference-Conditioned Subtask and Trajectory Generation; and (3) Satisfaction Metric Generation.
paragraphs.zh: 在 LIBERO 框架的基础上，LIBERO-PeRM 提供了一个可扩展的流程化数据生成管道，用于偏好学习和评估，具体如第 3 图所示；模型辅助生成与验证的细节见附录 C。 该管道包含三个阶段：（1）偏好选择与布局修改；（2）基于偏好的子任务与轨迹生成；以及（3）满意度指标生成。

sents.en: The pipeline consists of three stages: (1) Preference Selection and Layout Modification; (2) Preference-Conditioned Subtask and Trajectory Generation; and (3) Satisfaction Metric Generation.
sents.zh: 该管道包含三个阶段：（1）偏好选择与布局修改；（2）基于偏好的子任务与轨迹生成；以及（3）满意度指标生成。

paragraphs.en: Preference Selection and Layout Modification. The user first selects a preference instance and an initial LIBERO layout [ 23 ] . Given these inputs, the pipeline uses a VLM [ 72 ] to minimally modify the layout so the selected preference can be operationalized while limiting changes to the original scene. For Motion Preference and Skill Preference preferences, the layout and task language remain unchanged; the VLM only selects the target object or region, e.g., choosing the stove as the object to avoid for “avoid certain object” . For User Profile preferences, which may change the subtask plan, the pipeline makes minimal edits, such as adding a red object of the same category for a red-object preference, so preference-conditioned and no-preference trajectories can be generated in the same setting. The task language is also abstracted to cover both settings, ensuring that behavioral differences are driven by the preference rather than unrelated scene changes.
paragraphs.zh: 偏好选择与布局修改。 用户首先选择一个偏好实例和一个初始的 LIBERO 布局 [ 23 ] 。 基于这些输入，该流程使用 VLM [ 72 ] 对布局进行最小程度的修改，以便将所选偏好转化为可操作的形式，同时限制对原始场景的改动。 对于运动偏好和技能偏好，布局和任务语言保持不变；VLM 仅选择目标物体或区域，例如，在“避免特定物体”的情况下选择炉灶作为要避开的物体。 对于可能改变子任务计划的用户资料偏好，该流程会进行最小程度的编辑，例如为“红色物体偏好”添加同一类别的红色物体，从而能够在相同设置下生成受偏好影响和不受偏好影响的轨迹。 任务语言也被抽象化以涵盖两种设置，确保行为差异由偏好本身驱动，而非无关的场景变化。

paragraphs.en: Preference-Conditioned Subtask and Trajectory Generation. After the layout and task language are fixed, the pipeline uses a VLM with the task language and preference language to generate both a no-preference subtask plan and a preference-conditioned subtask plan. It then calls a library of pre-recorded heuristic skills to generate trajectory data. To construct each heuristic skill, we first collect one human demonstration for the skill, extract key waypoints, and use an OMPL planner [ 73 ] with randomized initial states to generate many successful trajectories. The generated trajectories are then smoothed; heuristic-skill parameters are manually offset-adjusted when needed. Empirically, we find more than 72% of skills require no offset adjustment across any task, suggesting the VLM-based edit is already very effective. Preferences are applied at different stages according to their type: User Profile affects subtask-plan generation via a prompt; Skill Preference affects skill selection, such as using pick_handle instead of a regular pick skill; and Motion Preference affects skill-level trajectory generation, such as reducing OMPL-sampled waypoints for the “speed up” preference.
paragraphs.zh: 偏好条件子任务与轨迹生成。 在布局与任务语言确定后，该流程使用一种结合任务语言和偏好语言的视觉语言模型（VLM），同时生成无偏好的子任务计划与偏好条件的子任务计划。 随后，它会调用一个预录制的启发式技能库来生成轨迹数据。 为构建每个启发式技能，我们首先收集该技能的一项人类演示，提取关键路径点，并使用一种随机化初始状态的 OMPL 规划器 [73] 生成大量成功轨迹。 生成的轨迹随后会被平滑处理；必要时，启发式技能的参数会通过手动偏移调整。 根据经验，我们发现超过 72% 的技能在任何任务中都不需要偏移调整，这表明基于 VLM 的编辑方法已经非常有效。 偏好会根据其类型在不同阶段应用：用户配置文件通过提示词影响子任务计划的生成；技能偏好影响技能的选择，例如使用“抓取把手”而非普通的抓取技能；运动偏好则影响技能层级的轨迹生成，例如为“加速”偏好减少 OMPL 采样的路径点。

paragraphs.en: Satisfaction Metric Generation. After preference-conditioned trajectories are generated, the pipeline constructs explicit preference satisfaction metrics for each selected preference. The form of each metric depends on the preference type. For Motion Preference , we directly compute satisfaction functions from trajectory quantities, such as the distance between the robot trajectory and the target object for the preference “avoid certain object” . For Skill Preference , we evaluate key waypoints and use VLM-based image checks to verify skill-specific execution, such as whether the object is grasped by its handle. For User Profile , we monitor the executed subtask plan, including which objects are manipulated, to verify that the plan adheres to the profile.
paragraphs.zh: 满意度指标生成。 在生成偏好条件化的轨迹后，该流程会为每个选定的偏好构建明确的偏好满意度指标。 每个指标的形式取决于偏好的类型。 对于运动偏好，我们直接从轨迹数据中计算满意度函数，例如，对于“避开特定物体”这一偏好，计算机器人轨迹与目标物体之间的距离。 对于技能偏好，我们会评估关键路径点，并使用基于 VLM 的图像检查来验证特定技能的执行情况，例如物体是否通过其把手被抓取。 对于用户画像，我们会监控已执行的子任务计划，包括哪些物体被操作，以验证该计划是否符合用户画像。

paragraphs.en: Because User Profile yields only discrete Satisfaction Scores, namely whether the profile-conditioned subtask is satisfied, whereas Motion Preference and Skill Preference can yield continuous Satisfaction Scores, we construct a mapping from Satisfaction Scores to Discrete Satisfaction Labels using trajectory statistics and human inspection; Appendix D details the review protocol. Specifically, each episode is mapped to a fixed four-level Discrete Satisfaction Label d ∈ { 0 , 1 / 4 , 3 / 4 , 1 } d\in\{0,1/4,3/4,1\} , independent of the number of pipeline-generated subtasks. A continuous Satisfaction Score, such as speed, is binned by trajectory statistics and then incorporated into this label. Raw Satisfaction Scores provide denser feedback for training, while Discrete Satisfaction Labels provide a more interpretable evaluation signal at inference time.
paragraphs.zh: 由于用户画像仅能产生离散的满意度分数，即判断由该画像条件约束的子任务是否完成，而运动偏好和技能偏好则能产生连续的满意度分数，因此我们基于轨迹统计和人工审核构建了一个从满意度分数到离散满意度标签的映射；附录 D 详细说明了审核流程。 具体而言，每个回合都会被映射到一个固定的四级离散满意度标签 d ∈ { 0 , 1 / 4 , 3 / 4 , 1 }，且该标签与流程中生成的子任务数量无关。 像速度这样的连续满意度分数会通过轨迹统计进行分箱处理，然后被整合到该标签中。 原始满意度分数能为训练提供更密集的反馈，而离散满意度标签则能在推理阶段提供更易于解释的评价信号。

paragraphs.en: Initial Human Validation. To assess the real-world plausibility of the selected preferences and the human-likeness of the generated demonstrations, we conducted a survey with 15 participants using a 10-point scale. Across all preference categories, the demonstrations received an average human-likeness score of 9.11, and the preferences received an average real-world plausibility score of 8.35. These results provide initial human validation of the benchmark design; Appendix D reports the protocol and category-level results.

paragraphs.en: Using the pipeline above, we generate five task suites: LIBERO-SinglePref, LIBERO-PrefScale, LIBERO-PrefConflict, LIBERO-PrefCompose, and LIBERO-ComprePref. We follow LIBERO terminology and call the inseparable combination of a task instruction, scene layout, and task-goal condition a mission . A LIBERO-PeRM task pairs one mission with one preference condition, which may be a specified preference or no preference; the 312 tasks include both preference-conditioned and no-preference tasks (see Figure 2 (b) for the proportions), with more than 100 trajectories per task on average and 40.8K rollout episodes in total. Randomized initial object positions, paraphrased instructions, and repeated executions increase rollout diversity but do not create additional tasks. The release prioritizes quality-controlled coverage over claiming the largest trajectory count; the procedural pipeline can extend it with more initial states and missions. Figure 2 (a-c) shows distributions over preference instances, task suites, and preference types, including no-preference tasks for comparison. Figure 2 (d) shows that episode horizons and trajectory fluency remain comparable to LIBERO. Each suite isolates a core capability for personalized manipulation, as summarized in Figure 1 .

paragraphs.en: LIBERO-SinglePref. This suite evaluates single-preference learning and execution. It contains 100 tasks and serves as the foundation for evaluating personalization. LIBERO-PrefScale. This suite evaluates how preference learning scales across demonstrations, tasks, and layouts. It supports controlled analysis of preference acquisition and generalization across tasks and layouts. It contains 100 tasks. LIBERO-PrefConflict. This suite evaluates policy behavior when preferences conflict with other preferences or with the task goal. Preference-preference conflicts pair the same layout and task with mutually conflicting single preferences, while task-preference conflicts pair no-preference task data with task-incompatible preference data. It contains 48 tasks. LIBERO-PrefCompose. This suite evaluates multi-preference learning and preference composition in a controlled two-preference setting. For each aligned layout-task pair, it provides four conditions: no preference, P A P_{A} , P B P_{B} , and P A + P B P_{A}+P_{B} , enabling controlled comparisons for composition and multi-preference learning. It contains 64 tasks. LIBERO-ComprePref. This suite rewrites prompts over tasks from the other suites so the preference must be inferred from contextual language rather than read from a separate explicit field. It includes explicit task-preference mixtures, where key preference words are preserved, and implicit preference reasoning, where contextual cues imply the preference without naming it. For example, “Put both the alphabet soup and the cream cheese box in the basket. Preference: speed up” becomes “Put both the alphabet soup and the cream cheese box in the basket. Guests will use them immediately.” Similarly, “Pick the mug by its handle” is conveyed as “The mug just came out of the microwave—the body is too hot to touch.” ComprePref reuses existing tasks, so its contextual prompts do not add to the 312-task count or the base-suite counts in Figure 2 (a). Appendix E gives a worked example; Appendix G describes the release and maintenance plan.

paragraphs.en: Task and Preference Metrics. We report two types of metrics: task success rate (SR), which measures task completion, and preference satisfaction (SA), which measures how well a preference is satisfied using the Discrete Satisfaction Label from Section 3.2 . The Discrete Satisfaction Label for episode n n is d n ∈ { 0 , 1 / 4 , 3 / 4 , 1 } d_{n}\in\{0,1/4,3/4,1\} , and 𝕀 ⁡ [ G ⁡ ( τ n ) ] \mathbb{I}[G(\tau_{n})] is its task-success indicator. We compute SA = 1 N ​ ∑ n = 1 N 𝕀 ⁡ [ G ⁡ ( τ n ) ] ​ d n \mathrm{SA}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}[G(\tau_{n})]d_{n} , so preference satisfaction contributes only when the task succeeds.
paragraphs.zh: 任务与偏好指标。 我们报告两类指标：任务成功率（SR），用于衡量任务完成度；以及偏好满意度（SA），通过第 3.2 节中的离散满意度标签来衡量偏好被满足的程度。 第 n 个回合的离散满意度标签为 d_n ∈ {0, 1/4, 3/4, 1}，而 𝕀[G(τ_n)] 是其任务成功指示符。 我们计算 SA = 1/N ∑_{n=1}^N 𝕀[G(τ_n)]d_n，因此只有当任务成功时，偏好满意度才会产生贡献。

paragraphs.en: Conflict Policy. For a task-preference conflict, completing the original task takes priority. For preference-preference conflicts, SA is computed using the higher of the two preference satisfaction scores for each episode, with task-failure episodes contributing zero satisfaction. These scoring conventions probe execution under inconsistent instructions; they do not evaluate conflict detection, preference weighting, or when a policy should ask the user for guidance.
paragraphs.zh: 冲突策略。 在任务与偏好发生冲突时，完成原始任务具有优先权。 在偏好与偏好发生冲突时，SA 的计算将基于每轮中两个偏好满足分数的较高值，而任务失败的轮次则不计入满足分。 这些评分规则旨在探究系统在指令不一致情况下的执行表现；它们并不评估冲突检测、偏好权重分配，或策略何时应请求用户指导。

paragraphs.en: Generalization. We evaluate in-domain, task-or-layout, and preference-level generalization using SR and SA. In-domain evaluation keeps the training tasks, preferences, and layouts with small object-position perturbations. Task-or-layout generalization changes either the task or layout, while preference-level generalization changes tasks under unseen layouts while keeping the preference unchanged.

paragraphs.en: Finding. Across all data scales, in-domain preference-conditioned behavior is learned consistently well. For in-domain preference learning, increasing layout diversity is more effective than simply increasing the number of demonstrations. Notably, adding matched no-preference data further improves learning even without increasing layout diversity, suggesting that such data helps decouple preference-conditioned behavior from task/layout-specific cues.
paragraphs.zh: 发现。 在所有数据规模下，领域内偏好条件行为都能被一致且良好地学习。 对于领域内偏好学习而言，增加布局多样性比单纯增加演示示例数量更为有效。 值得注意的是，即使不增加布局多样性，添加匹配的无偏好数据也能进一步提升学习效果，这表明此类数据有助于将偏好条件行为与任务或布局相关的特定线索解耦。

paragraphs.en: Figure 4 provides detailed evidence for these observations. First, the in-domain SR and SA curves are closely aligned across data scales, indicating strong in-domain preference learning: successful executions usually also satisfy the specified preferences. Second, at the fixed 2.25K scale, L1-L3 use the same demonstration budget but increase the number of layouts, and the improvement from L1 to L3 shows that broader layout coverage is more effective than denser demonstrations within fewer layouts. Third, L4 uses the same layout setting as L2 but adds matched no-preference missions; its improvement over L2 suggests that no-preference data benefits learning beyond increasing layout diversity, likely by helping separate task execution from preference-conditioned behavior.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a comprehensive benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation. By treating preferences as a first-class building block alongside tasks and layouts, LIBERO-PeRM provides five task suites that isolate and evaluate preference learning under single-preference, scaling, conflict, composition, and comprehensive preference reasoning settings. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Compared with sequential adaptation, mixed training better preserves no-preference behavior and improves contextual-prompt robustness, but it weakens motion-preference performance relative to preference-only LoRA. Preference learning benefits more from layout diversity and same-layout no-preference data than denser demonstrations, but generalization to unseen layouts and different tasks remains difficult. Composition is only partially observed, decomposition fails, and conflicts often degrade execution instead of producing resolution.
paragraphs.zh: 在这项工作中，我们提出了 LIBERO-PeRM，一个用于个性化机器人操作的综合性基准。 通过将偏好与任务及布局一同视为一等构建模块，LIBERO-PeRM 提供了五个任务套件，分别针对单一偏好、扩展性、冲突、组合以及综合偏好推理等场景，对偏好学习进行隔离和评估。 实验表明，当前的 VLA 策略在零样本个性化方面存在困难，而 SFT 则使偏好具有可学习性。 与顺序适应相比，混合训练能更好地保留无偏好行为并提升上下文提示的鲁棒性，但相较于仅针对偏好的 LoRA，其运动偏好表现有所减弱。 偏好学习从布局多样性和相同布局下的无偏好数据中获益更多，而非更密集的动作演示，但向未见过的布局和不同任务的泛化仍然困难。 组合过程仅被部分观察到，分解未能成功，而冲突通常会降低执行效果，而非产生解决方案。

paragraphs.en: Limitations and Future Work. LIBERO-PeRM instantiates predefined, language-expressible, automatically measurable preferences in simulation. It therefore excludes implicit preference inference, interaction history, non-linguistic signals, and open-ended or evolving preferences. Its generated demonstrations may contain pipeline- and skill-library-specific biases despite randomized initial states, multiple missions per preference, and human review. The current composition suite combines only two preferences, and the conflict suite does not test conflict detection or clarification. Finally, the human survey provides only initial validation; no real-robot or longitudinal user study is included. Future work could extend LIBERO-PeRM in directions ranging from three-or-more-preference settings to non-linguistic preference signals, human-in-the-loop preference acquisition, preference weighting and when-to-ask decisions, and real-robot evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 局限性与未来工作。 LIBERO-PeRM 在模拟中具体化了预定义、可用语言表达且可自动测量的偏好。 因此，它排除了隐式偏好推断、交互历史、非语言信号以及开放或不断演变的偏好。 尽管初始状态是随机化的、每个偏好包含多个任务并经过人类审核，其生成的示范仍可能包含特定于流程管道和技能库的偏见。 当前的组合套件仅结合了两种偏好，而冲突套件并未测试冲突检测或澄清功能。 最后，人类调查仅提供初步验证；研究未包含真实机器人测试或纵向用户研究。 未来的工作可以从多种方向扩展 LIBERO-PeRM，包括设置三种或更多偏好、引入非语言偏好信号、实现人在回路中的偏好获取、偏好权重分配与提问时机决策，以及进行真实机器人评估。

sents.en: Future work could extend LIBERO-PeRM in directions ranging from three-or-more-preference settings to non-linguistic preference signals, human-in-the-loop preference acquisition, preference weighting and when-to-ask decisions, and real-robot evaluation.

paragraphs.en: LIBERO-PeRM is built from procedurally generated preference-conditioned tasks, layouts, trajectories, and evaluation signals in simulation. Human feedback is used to review generated data and validate preference plausibility, but no personal data or real-world user logs are released or used as policy-training data. Its intended use is research on personalized robotic manipulation, including preference learning, generalization, composition, and conflict handling. Our dataset construction process is designed to reduce ethical and legal risk. We build on LIBERO [ 23 ] scenes and simulator assets, then generate preference-conditioned variants through minimal layout edits, procedural trajectory generation, and automatic preference metrics. Preference descriptions, satisfaction rules, and benchmark annotations are created for research use rather than copied from external products or commercial systems. Any public release should preserve attribution to upstream assets and follow the licenses and terms of use of LIBERO and other dependencies. The benchmark also has important limitations. Our preference metrics only capture observable execution outcomes in simulation and cannot represent open-ended, private, or highly subjective human preferences. As a result, LIBERO-PeRM should not be treated as a substitute for human evaluation in safety-critical or real-world personalized deployment. We intend this benchmark to support controlled scientific evaluation, not direct real-world decision making.
paragraphs.zh: LIBERO-PeRM 由在模拟环境中通过程序生成的、基于偏好的任务、布局、轨迹和评估信号构建而成。 人类反馈被用于审查生成的数据并验证偏好的合理性，但不会发布任何个人数据或真实世界的用户日志，也不会将其用作策略训练数据。 其预期用途是开展个性化机器人操作研究，包括偏好学习、泛化、组合以及冲突处理。 我们的数据集构建过程旨在降低伦理和法律风险。 我们在 LIBERO [23] 的场景和模拟器资源基础上，通过最小程度的布局修改、程序化轨迹生成以及自动偏好指标来生成基于偏好的变体。 偏好描述、满意度规则和基准标注均为研究用途而创建，而非从外部产品或商业系统中复制而来。 任何公开发布都应保留对上游资源的引用，并遵守 LIBERO 及其他依赖项的许可协议和使用条款。 该基准也存在一些重要的局限性。 我们的偏好指标仅能捕捉模拟环境中可观察的执行结果，无法代表开放式的、私密的或高度主观的人类偏好。 因此，不应将 LIBERO-PeRM 视为在安全关键或真实世界个性化部署中替代人类评估的工具。 我们设计此基准的初衷是支持受控的科学评估，而非直接用于现实世界的决策。

paragraphs.en: We select a preference only if it satisfies five criteria: 1) expressible in natural language; 2) can be grounded in existing LIBERO [ 23 ] scenes; 3) satisfiable without changing the task goal; 4) measurable by an automatic preference metric; and 5) reusable across multiple tasks or layouts. Examples include the Motion Preference preference “speed up” , measured by execution steps; the Skill Preference preference “pick up an object by its handle” , measured by waypoints and contact points; and the User Profile preference “prefer dairy product” , measured by the executed subgoal. We exclude preferences that require scene-external information, unsafe or task-infeasible behavior, or subjective judgments that cannot be mapped to observable execution outcomes.
paragraphs.zh: 我们仅在选择偏好满足以下五个标准时才会采纳：1）能用自然语言表达；2）能基于现有的 LIBERO [ 23 ] 场景进行落地；3）在不改变任务目标的前提下可满足；4）能通过自动偏好指标进行衡量；以及 5）能在多个任务或布局中重复使用。 示例包括运动偏好“加速”，通过执行步数进行衡量；技能偏好“通过提手拿起物体”，通过路径点和接触点进行衡量；以及用户画像偏好“偏好乳制品”，通过已执行的子目标进行衡量。 我们排除那些需要场景外部信息、涉及不安全或任务不可行的行为，或是无法映射到可观察执行结果的主观判断的偏好。

paragraphs.en: We use Claude Code with an Opus-family model and Gemini as backends for three model-assisted stages. In layout editing , the model receives a BDDL scene specification, preference language, object geometry, and spatial constraints, and proposes a modified BDDL layout. In personalized planning , it receives the original task and preference instructions, baseline plan, available objects and skills, and a scene image, and returns a sequence of (skill, object) pairs plus required, prohibited, and ordering constraints. In image inspection , independent VLM judgments assess task completion and visually observable preference compliance from rollout frames.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 Claude Code，并采用 Opus 系列模型和 Gemini 作为后端，以支持三个模型辅助阶段。 在布局编辑阶段，模型接收 BDDL 场景规范、偏好语言、对象几何形状和空间约束，并提出修改后的 BDDL 布局方案。 在个性化规划阶段，模型接收原始任务与偏好指令、基准计划、可用对象与技能以及场景图像，并返回一系列（技能，对象）对，以及所需的、禁止的和对序约束。 在图像检查阶段，独立的 VLM 判断会基于执行过程中的帧画面评估任务完成度及视觉上可观察到的偏好合规性。

paragraphs.en: Inspired by single- and multi-agent evaluations [ 76 , 77 , 78 ] , the layout and plan candidates follow a generate-and-trial loop: each proposal is instantiated and tested in simulation, and any candidate violating the output format, physical constraints, task-success condition, or preference constraints is rejected. The observed failure is included when generating a revised candidate. The reported VLM failure rate in each stage was below 23%. For image inspection, inconsistent independent judgments are flagged for re-evaluation rather than accepted directly. Image judgments are restricted to visible properties such as contact location, approach direction, gripper orientation, and final placement. Motion speed, acceleration, trajectory smoothness, and clearance height are instead measured with trajectory-based geometric or kinematic metrics.
paragraphs.zh: 受单智能体和多智能体评估 [76, 77, 78] 的启发，布局与方案候选遵循“生成-测试”循环：每个提案都会被实例化并在模拟中测试；任何违反输出格式、物理约束、任务成功条件或偏好约束的候选方案都将被拒绝。 在生成修订后的候选方案时，会将观察到的失败情况纳入考虑。 各阶段报告的 VLM 失败率均低于 23%。 对于图像检查，不一致的独立判断会被标记以供重新评估，而非直接接受。 图像判断仅限于可见属性，例如接触位置、接近方向、夹爪朝向和最终放置位置。 运动速度、加速度、轨迹平滑度和离地高度则通过基于轨迹的几何或运动学指标进行测量。

paragraphs.en: Human contributors participated in three stages: 1) providing one reference demonstration for each newly introduced skill; 2) inspecting sampled generated demonstrations together with their satisfaction labels and metrics; and 3) rating preference plausibility and demonstration human-likeness. Before beginning, contributors received common instructions and task-specific training. Contributors were assigned to different portions of the generated data, after which a second group cross-reviewed the demonstrations and labels. Disputed cases were jointly re-examined before inclusion; the initial reviewer disagreement rate was 11.8%. All participants provided informed consent, and contributors were credited according to their level of involvement.

paragraphs.en: For initial user validation, 15 participants rated the selected preferences and their demonstrations on a 10-point scale along two dimensions: real-world preference plausibility , whether each preference was plausible and applicable in a household setting; and human-likeness of demonstrations , how closely the corresponding demonstration resembled how a human would naturally perform the task while satisfying the preference. Table 7 summarizes 37 preferences in three categories. These results provide initial evidence of plausibility and human-likeness, but they do not substitute for real-robot, longitudinal, or larger-scale user studies.

paragraphs.en: Underlying task: Put the white mug on the left plate. Explicit preference: Pick by the handle. Input prompt: Put the white mug on the left plate. The mug just came out of the microwave—the body is too hot to touch. Implied behavior: Grasp the handle while completing the same placement task. What stays fixed: The task goal, scene, and preference evaluator. SR evaluates the original placement goal; SA uses the original handle-grasp preference label with task-success gating. What changes: The language supplied to the policy conveys the preference through context instead of a separate explicit preference field.
paragraphs.zh: 底层任务：将白色马克杯放在左边的盘子上。 显式偏好：通过手柄抓取。 输入提示：将白色马克杯放在左边的盘子上。 这个马克杯刚从微波炉里拿出来——杯身太烫，无法触摸。 隐含行为：在完成相同的放置任务时，同时握住手柄。 保持不变的部分：任务目标、场景和偏好评估器。 SR 评估原始的放置目标；SA 使用原始的手柄抓取偏好标签，并结合任务成功机制进行判断。 发生变化的部分：提供给策略的语言通过上下文传达偏好，而不是通过独立的显式偏好字段。

paragraphs.en: A second example replaces the explicit preference “speed up” with “Guests will use them immediately” for the task of putting alphabet soup and a cream cheese box in a basket. The motion preference is still evaluated from the trajectory, not from a still image. These contextual prompts assess grounding of a specified benchmark preference; they do not establish recovery of an individual user’s unobserved preference history.
paragraphs.zh: 第二个例子将明确偏好“加快”替换为“客人会立即使用它们”，用于将字母汤和奶油奶酪盒放入篮子的任务中。 运动偏好仍然根据轨迹进行评估，而不是根据静态图像进行评估。 这些上下文提示评估的是特定基准偏好的落地情况；它们并未确立对单个用户未观察到的偏好历史的恢复。

paragraphs.en: Adding a standard preference requires one human reference demonstration and a natural-language description of its satisfaction metric for the preference-conditioned generation pipeline, followed by approximately three to five validation trials for each applicable task. For a preference applied to roughly five tasks, the observed manual effort is about 20 minutes on average; demonstration generation then proceeds automatically. This estimate covers preferences expressible through the current scene representation, skill library, and automatic programmable metrics. Preferences requiring a new skill or non-observable feedback incur additional work.
paragraphs.zh: 添加一个标准偏好需要一次人类参考演示，以及对其满足度指标的自然语言描述，用于偏好条件生成流程，随后还需针对每个适用任务进行大约三到五次验证试验。 对于应用于约五个任务的偏好，观察到的平均人工投入时间约为 20 分钟；之后演示生成将自动进行。 该估算涵盖了可通过当前场景表示、技能库和自动可编程指标表达的偏好。 需要新技能或不可观测反馈的偏好会增加额外工作量。

sents.en: Preferences requiring a new skill or non-observable feedback incur additional work.
sents.zh: 需要新技能或不可观测反馈的偏好会增加额外工作量。

paragraphs.en: For example, to add a preference for grasping a mug by its handle, a user provides one reference demonstration and a natural-language description of the satisfaction metric: the robot should grasp the handle rather than the mug body. The original mug-placement goal remains unchanged. The user then runs approximately three to five validation trials for each applicable task to check whether the generated trajectories follow the preference and whether the metric correctly evaluates grasp location. After validation, the pipeline automatically generates additional demonstrations.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，若要增加优先抓取杯子把手的偏好，用户会提供一个参考演示，并用自然语言描述满意度指标：机器人应抓取把手，而非杯身。 杯子放置的原始目标保持不变。 随后，用户对每个适用任务运行大约三到五次验证试验，以检查生成的轨迹是否符合该偏好，以及该指标是否正确评估了抓取位置。 验证结束后，流程会自动生成额外的演示。

paragraphs.en: The benchmark has five evaluation suites. The 312 tasks include both preference-conditioned and no-preference tasks across SinglePref (100), PrefScale (100), PrefConflict (48), and PrefCompose (64); ComprePref reuses tasks with contextual prompts and does not add new mission-preference combinations to this count. Demonstrations are generated trajectories used as training/reference data; evaluation rollouts are executions of the evaluated policy and are not additional benchmark tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 该基准测试包含五个评估套件。 这 312 项任务涵盖了 SinglePref（100）、PrefScale（100）、PrefConflict（48）和 PrefCompose（64）中的偏好条件型和无偏好型任务；ComprePref 会复用带有上下文提示的任务，但不会在此总数中新增任务与偏好的组合。 演示是作为训练/参考数据使用的生成轨迹；评估执行则是被评估策略的运行过程，并非额外的基准测试任务。
